sections.heading: Hail Last Night, a Letter This Week, and No Idea What Comes Next
body: Picture the morning after a bad storm. You can see a few shingles in the yard, and a neighbor already has a ladder against his house. Your insurance company has sent a form, and you don't know what the adjuster looks for or who is supposed to tell you the next step.
This is the moment to call someone who has already walked other Peoria homeowners through it. Nobody should have to learn roofing and insurance in the same week.

sections.heading: Jose Looks at the Roof. Amanda Walks You Through the Claim.
body: Two people handle your job from the first call to the last day. Jose comes out, gets a look at the roof and explains what it needs. If a repair is all it needs, a repair is what you hear.
Amanda sits down with you on the paperwork. She explains each step of the claim and what to expect while the work is scheduled, and she deals with your insurance company or agent alongside you.
We can't tell you what your insurance company will decide. We can make sure you know what is happening while they decide.

sections.heading: Fixing a Roof Is Stressful Enough Without Guessing
body: Most people hire a roofer once or twice in their lives. You're dealing with a leak or a storm, a claim and a stranger on your roof, all in the same month.
What helps is having someone keep track for you: a person who answers your questions as they come up and tells you what happens next. We want that to be our job, on top of the roof itself.

sections.quote: Absolutely the best experience I've ever had a home improvement/maintenence business. Getting work on the house is stressful and Amanda and Jose make it as stress free as possible.
sections.name: Christopher L.

sections.heading: One Storm Can Hit the Roof, the Siding and the Gutters
body: Hail doesn't stop at the shingles. It dents gutters, and wind can leave siding, fascia and soffit needing work too. We install siding and gutters along with roofs, so one team can cover what the storm hit.
Handling it together also means one set of people to call. You don't have to explain your house to three different companies, or wonder which one is waiting on the other.

sections.intro: Roof replacement comes first, because it's the job most calls turn into. Repairs, siding, gutters and metal roofs follow.

sections.heading: What Brings Peoria Homeowners to the Phone
body: Any of these is a good reason to ask for a free look.

items.title: A storm went through and nobody has looked at the roof
items.text: Hail damage can sit on a roof for months before it leaks. A look now is easier than a ceiling stain later.

items.title: A stain on the ceiling after a heavy rain
items.text: Water often shows up a long way from where it gets in. It may be a repair, not a whole new roof, and you find out by getting up there.

items.title: A cracked seal around a vent pipe
items.text: A small gap can let water in without any storm at all. Fixing a vent seal is a job we do.

items.title: A letter from your insurance company
items.text: Call us, and Amanda can explain the steps that come next.

items.title: A roof that has simply gotten old
items.text: When shingles are worn across the whole roof, patching stops making sense. Jose tells you where yours stands.

sections.quote: Jose actually came to inspect our roof three times. The first when we were thinking of replacing it, the second after a hail storm, and the third when the insurance tried to short change us. … Should this Illinois weather damage my roof again, I know who I am calling.
sections.name: Robert T.

sections.heading: When the Adjuster Is Coming, You Aren't Alone With It
body: Meeting an adjuster for the first time is easier when someone has told you what the visit is for. Amanda explains the claim process and what to expect, so you know what to ask.
Our part is the roof, the explaining and the paperwork. Coverage and settlement stay between you and your insurance company, and your agent is the right person for questions about your policy.

sections.heading: The Day the Crew Is There

sections.heading: Replace It or Repair It?
body: A new roof is a big bill, so the first question is whether you need one at all. A failed seal around a vent or a worn patch is a repair, and we do repairs.
Hail damage spread across the roof, shingles worn out everywhere, or leaks in more than one place point to replacement. After looking over the whole roof, Jose says which it is.

sections.heading: Signs a Roof Is Past Patching
body: Not every worn roof needs replacing, and not every leak is the roof's fault. These are the signs that point toward a new roof instead of another repair.

items.title: Cracked, curling or missing shingles in many places
items.text: One lifted tab is a repair. The same damage across most of the roof is a different problem.

items.title: Granules collecting in the gutters
items.text: Shingles lose their gritty top layer as they wear out and when hail bruises them. It washes down to the gutter and the downspout.

items.title: Leaks in more than one spot
items.text: A single leak often traces to one vent or one flashing. Stains in several rooms can mean the roof itself is failing.

items.title: Soft or sagging areas
items.text: A roof that feels spongy underfoot may have damaged wood underneath, and that takes more than new shingles.

items.title: Dents on gutters and vents after a storm
items.text: Hail that dents metal can bruise the shingles beside it, even when the roof looks fine from the yard.

sections.heading: After Hail or Wind, There Is a Claim Running Beside the Roof
body: You're managing two things at once: the roof and the paperwork. Amanda explains each step of the claim and what to expect while the work is scheduled.

A claim can take weeks or months. Questions come up in the meantime, and she answers them. Coverage and settlement are between you and your insurance company, and we don't guess at what they will decide.

sections.heading: Questions About Replacing a Roof

items.q: How much does a roof replacement cost?
items.a: It depends on the size and shape of the roof and the material you choose, so we don't quote a number sight unseen. Call (309) 567-8236 and ask for the free estimate.

items.q: Will my insurance pay for a new roof?
items.a: That is between you and your insurance company, and your agent can tell you what your policy includes. We explain the claim steps and what to expect along the way.

items.q: Do I need to replace the whole roof?
items.a: Not always. One leaking vent seal or a worn spot is a repair. The whole roof gets looked at first.

items.q: Can the gutters be replaced at the same time?
items.a: Yes. Gutters, gutter guards, fascia and soffit can be done with the roof.
It depends on the weather and our schedule. Call, and we'll tell you where things stand.

closing.text: Your customers already describe how you work: Jose on the roof, Amanda on the claim, a clean yard at the end. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we'll walk you through this demo and plan your new site.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your contact block and your Google listing show (309) 567-8236, while your Call or Text button dials (309) 316-3652, so which number is live, and who answers each one? This demo uses the Google number.
Your About page says BBB A+ accredited, while we found no BBB profile for you, so is the accreditation current, and should it go on your listings?

A search result for your Angi listing says you don't offer emergency service, while your site says nothing either way and a review has Jose coming out on a Sunday, so what should every listing say about after-hours calls?

offer.heading: The offer we'd build with you
offer.text: This is a proposal for you to decide on, not something JG Roofing does today. It is a one-page claim and job timeline, handed to the homeowner before the tear-off, with each step in order. As far as we found, none of the top Peoria roofers we checked offers one.
points: Amanda already explains the claim step by step. Put the steps on one page the homeowner keeps: the adjuster visit, what the insurance company sends, and who to call with a question.
Add the date, the timeframe and the cleanup on the same page, so the week of the work holds no surprises.
Say plainly what the page leaves out: coverage and settlement belong to the insurance company. Terms are yours to set.
